mainTopic: A wall piece jutting across a מבוי entrance: when it is a לחי, when it needs another לחי, and how עומד מרובה על הפרוץ and ספק דרבנן make the extra לחי unnecessary
overview: This amud finishes the ruling of רמי בר חמא about a piece of wall that juts out across the entrance of a מבוי. If it juts out less than four אמות, it counts as a לחי. If it juts out four אמות, it counts as a small מבוי of its own and needs another לחי. רב פפא says the extra לחי goes on the opposite side, and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע allows it next to the first one if it is a visibly different size. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע then limits the ruling to an eight-אמה-wide מבוי. In a seven-wide מבוי, the alley is permitted anyway by עומד מרובה על הפרוץ, which he proves with a קל וחומר from a חצר. The גמרא challenges that proof and defends it by explaining that he holds, on his own view, that a מבוי also allows a breach of ten. רב אשי goes further and says even an eight-wide מבוי needs no extra לחי. Either the wall is bigger, or the gap is bigger and the wall is a לחי, or the two are equal, which is a ספק דרבנן and is ruled leniently. The amud ends by opening a new statement of רב about a breached מבוי, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Less than four cubits is a side post, four cubits is an alleyway
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of the ruling of רמי בר חמא. A לחי that juts out less than four אמות counts as a לחי. A לחי that juts out four אמות turns its covered stretch into its own מבוי, and that stretch needs another לחי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it sticks out less than four אמות, it is treated as a לחי, and no other לחי is needed to permit carrying. If it sticks out four אמות, it is treated as a מבוי, and another לחי is needed to permit carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a rule that began on the previous amud: how far a side post sticks into the alley decides whether it counts as a לחי or as a small alley of its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Four אמות is the minimum length of a מבוי. So once the post sticks out a full four אמות, that stretch has the size of a real alleyway. Instead of permitting the alley, it becomes a new alley that needs its own permit. Under four אמות, it is too short to be a מבוי, so it simply works as the לחי.

keyTerms.meaning: A side post placed at the entrance of an alley to permit carrying inside
An alleyway, closed on three sides and open to the public domain on one side
Four cubits, the minimum length of a מבוי
Is judged as, is treated in the category of
To permit it (for carrying)

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The case is a לחי that juts out from the side wall across the width of the alley's entrance, partly closing the opening. The 'four אמות' is how far it extends across the opening, not how tall it is.

phrases.english: Less than four cubits
it is treated as a side post,
and no other side post is needed to permit it.
Four cubits
it is treated as an alleyway,
and another side post is needed to permit it.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּחוֹת מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת נִידּוֹן מִשּׁוּם לֶחִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continuation of the ruling of רמי בר חמא on the previous amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A לחי under four אמות long works as a לחי. At four אמות it becomes a מבוי needing an additional לחי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule sets up everything that follows: the placement of the extra לחי and the limit of the rule to an eight-אמה מבוי.

steps.title: Where does the extra side post go?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the second לחי should be placed. If it goes right next to the first one, it looks like the first one was just made wider.
steps.simpleTranslation: That extra לחי, where does he set it up? If he sets it up next to the first one, it looks like he is just adding on to the first one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question about the rule just stated, and points out a problem with the obvious answer. This sets up the next two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A לחי works because people can see it as a marker. A second post placed flush against the first one blends in and looks like one wider post. Then no separate לחי is noticeable for the new 'mini-alley'.

keyTerms.meaning: Where does he stand it up / place it?
Next to it, together with it
He is merely adding on (to the existing one)

phrases.english: That side post, where does he place it?
If he places it next to the first one,
he is just adding on to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to carry out the requirement of 'another לחי' stated in step 1
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The correct placement of the additional לחי so that it is recognizable as a separate לחי

steps.title: Place it on the opposite side
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the second לחי goes on the other side of the alley, by the opposite wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: He sets it up on the other side.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question by moving the second לחי away from the first one, to the opposite wall of the alley.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting it on the far side removes the problem completely. It cannot be mistaken for an extension of the first post, so it clearly serves as its own לחי.

keyTerms.meaning: On the other side

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
He places it on the other side.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא דְּמוֹקֵי לֵיהּ לְאִידַּךְ גִּיסָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra לחי is placed on the opposite wall of the מבוי

steps.title: It may go alongside if it is visibly different
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says the second לחי may even stand next to the first one, as long as it is taller or shorter so that it stands out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said: You can even say he sets it up next to the first one, as long as he makes it bigger or smaller.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different answer. Placing the second לחי next to the first one is fine if it is made visibly different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern in step 2 was only that the second post would blend in. If it is noticeably taller or shorter (or thicker or thinner) than the first, it is clearly a separate post. So the problem is solved without moving it to the other side.

keyTerms.meaning: You may even say
That he adds to it (makes it larger)
That he reduces it (makes it smaller)

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
You may even say that he places it next to the first one,
as long as he adds to it or reduces it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 2, more lenient than רב פפא in step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra לחי may stand next to the first if it differs in size, making it recognizable
steps.whatToRemember: Two ways to place the extra לחי: רב פפא puts it on the opposite side, and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע allows it next to the first one if it is a different size.

steps.title: The rule applies only to an eight-cubit alley; a seven-cubit alley is permitted anyway
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע limits the ruling of רמי בר חמא to a מבוי eight אמות wide. In a seven-אמה-wide מבוי, the four-אמה post closes most of the entrance, so the alley is permitted because of עומד מרובה על הפרוץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said: We only said this rule about a מבוי eight אמות wide. But in a מבוי seven אמות wide, it is permitted because the standing part is greater than the open part.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now limits the original rule from step 1, showing a case where no extra לחי is needed at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a seven-wide alley, a post sticking in four אמות leaves only three open, so the closed part is bigger than the gap. That side counts as a wall with a doorway, and the alley is permitted without any לחי. In an eight-wide alley it is four closed and four open, which is not 'more closed', so the rule of step 1 still applies and another לחי is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this in the case of (a limiting formula)
The standing (closed) part is greater than the breached (open) part
It is permitted
The open, breached section

steps.confusionAlert: In the seven-אמה case, the post is not permitting the alley as a לחי. It permits the alley by closing off most of the opening, a completely different reason.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that עומד מרובה על הפרוץ can permit an alley on its own, and it narrows the ruling of רמי בר חמא to alleys eight אמות wide or more.
steps.whatToRemember: The four-אמה post needs an extra לחי only in a מבוי of eight or more. In a seven-wide מבוי, the closed part outweighs the open part, so it is permitted anyway.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
We said this only about an alleyway eight cubits wide.
But in an alleyway seven cubits wide
it is permitted because the standing part is greater than the breached part.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the base ruling in step 1 and limits its scope by alley width
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra-לחי requirement applies only in an eight-אמה מבוי. In a seven-אמה מבוי, the alley is permitted through עומד מרובה על הפרוץ.

steps.title: A courtyard proves that an alley works the same way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports step 5 with a קל וחומר: a חצר, which is stricter, is permitted by עומד מרובה על הפרוץ, so a מבוי, which is more lenient, should certainly be permitted that way too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this comes from a קל וחומר from a courtyard. A courtyard cannot be permitted with a side post or a crossbeam, yet it is permitted when the standing part is more than the open part. An alley can be permitted with a side post or a crossbeam. So isn't it logical that an alley is permitted when the standing part is more than the open part?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the ruling from step 5 that a mostly-closed מבוי entrance is enough. It argues from the easier-to-see case of a חצר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חצר needs real walls, because a לחי or קורה does not help it. A מבוי is treated more leniently, since even a small לחי or קורה can permit it. If even the strict חצר is permitted when most of the wall is standing, then the lenient מבוי should certainly be permitted the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a stricter case to a lighter case (or the reverse): if it is true there, it is surely true here
A courtyard shared by several houses
A crossbeam placed over the entrance of an alley
Becomes permitted, meaning one may carry inside it
Is it not logical? (the closing words of a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: And it is a kal vachomer from a courtyard:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה חָצֵר שֶׁאֵינָהּ נִיתֶּרֶת בְּלֶחִי וְקוֹרָה —
phrases.english: Just as a courtyard, which is not permitted by a side post or crossbeam,
is permitted when the standing part is more than the open part,
an alley, which is permitted by a side post or crossbeam,
is it not logical that it is permitted
when the standing part is more than the open part?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the rule in step 5 that a seven-אמה-wide מבוי is permitted by עומד מרובה על הפרוץ
steps.raayaObject: A מבוי is permitted when most of its entrance is closed
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from a חצר, which is permitted by עומד מרובה על הפרוץ even though a לחי or קורה cannot permit it

steps.title: But a courtyard is more lenient about breaches
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר is attacked. A חצר stays permitted with a breach of up to ten אמות, but a מבוי becomes forbidden with a breach of only four טפחים. So the חצר is not stricter in every way.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a courtyard? Its breach can be up to ten. Can you say the same about an alley, which becomes forbidden with a breach of only four?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the קל וחומר from step 6. It shows that in one important way a חצר is actually easier than a מבוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if one case is stricter in every relevant way. A חצר is permitted even with a gap of up to ten אמות, while a מבוי is ruined by a gap of four טפחים. Since this very issue is about gaps, the חצר cannot teach us about the מבוי.

keyTerms.meaning: "What about X, which has this feature?" The standard formula for breaking a קל וחומר
A breach or gap in a wall
"Will you say?" Can you really apply this to the other case?

steps.confusionAlert: The 'ten' for a חצר means ten אמות, but the 'four' for a מבוי means four טפחים (handbreadths), which is a much smaller measure. That big difference is what makes the מבוי stricter here.

phrases.english: What about a courtyard, whose breach can be up to ten [cubits],
will you say the same of an alley, whose breach is [only] four [handbreadths]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Breaks the קל וחומר of step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר from חצר to מבוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חצר is more lenient than a מבוי about breaches (ten versus four), so it cannot be called the stricter case

steps.title: He holds an alley also allows a breach of ten
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע holds a מבוי, like a חצר, can have a breach of up to ten. So the חצר is not more lenient, and the קל וחומר works.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע holds that an alley also has a breach limit of ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rescues the קל וחומר by saying the author of step 5 does not accept the 'four' rule for a מבוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in step 7 depended on a מבוי being stricter about gaps. If רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע holds that a מבוי also allows a gap of up to ten, that difference disappears. Then the חצר is again stricter overall, and the קל וחומר stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (this opinion)
Also

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua holds:
an alley also, its breach is up to ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the speaker's position: he rejects the premise of the challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees a מבוי is forbidden with a breach of four, so the חצר is more lenient
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, a מבוי also allows a breach of up to ten, so the קל וחומר holds

steps.title: But this discussion follows רב הונא, who says four
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: this whole discussion follows the view of רב הונא, and רב הונא holds that a מבוי's breach limit is four. So how can רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע say ten?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom are we saying all this? According to רב הונא. But doesn't רב הונא hold that an alley's breach is four?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 8. It points out that the discussion follows רב הונא, who holds the 'four' rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sugya is built on the opinion of רב הונא. רב הונא holds that a מבוי is ruined by a gap of four. If רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע is working inside רב הונא's system, he should not be able to say 'ten'.

keyTerms.meaning: "According to whom are we saying this?"
"But doesn't...?" Introduces a contradiction
He holds

phrases.english: According to whom are we saying this?
According to Rav Huna.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַב הוּנָא פִּרְצָתוֹ בְּאַרְבַּע סְבִירָא לֵיהּ?!
phrases.english: But doesn't Rav Huna hold that its breach is four?!

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע holds a מבוי's breach is ten
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The sugya follows רב הונא, and רב הונא explicitly holds the breach of a מבוי is four

steps.title: He is giving his own opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע is not explaining רב הונא's view. He is stating his own opinion, so he can disagree with רב הונא about breaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע is stating his own reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the problem by saying רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע speaks for himself, not for רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A later אמורא does not have to follow an earlier one. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע holds his own view that a מבוי allows a breach of ten. So the קל וחומר from a חצר works according to him, and his ruling in step 5 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He is stating his own reasoning, not someone else's

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, a seven-אמה-wide מבוי is permitted by עומד מרובה על הפרוץ. This is learned by a קל וחומר from a חצר. The proof works because he holds, on his own and against רב הונא, that a מבוי also allows a breach of ten.

phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua
is stating his own reasoning.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Separating the speaker's own view from the view of the earlier authority
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע must follow רב הונא's 'four' rule
steps.terutzMaskana: He states his own view that a breach of ten is allowed in a מבוי, so his קל וחומר stands

steps.title: רב אשי: even an eight-wide alley needs no extra side post
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says that even in a מבוי eight אמות wide, a four-אמה wall piece at the entrance is enough, because either way the מבוי is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Even if you say the alley is eight אמות wide, it still does not need a לחי. Whichever way you look at it: if the standing part is bigger, the alley is permitted because the standing part is more than the open part. If the open part is bigger, the wall piece is small enough to be treated as a לחי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי goes one step further than רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע and says even an eight-אמה-wide מבוי is fine without an extra לחי. He proves it by showing that both possible measurements lead to a permitted מבוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In an eight-wide entrance, a wall piece of about four אמות is right at the halfway mark, so we cannot be sure which part is bigger. רב אשי says it does not matter. If the wall is bigger, עומד מרובה על הפרוץ permits the מבוי. If the opening is bigger, the wall piece must be under four אמות, and that is narrow enough to count as a לחי, so the מבוי is permitted that way.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you look at it. Both possible options lead to the same result.
When the standing wall is more than the open gap, the area counts as closed.
Is bigger, is more.
A side post at the entrance of a מבוי that allows carrying inside it.
Is judged as, is treated as.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a classic way the גמרא argues: when we cannot tell which of two facts is true, it shows that both lead to the same law.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Even if you say in an alley of eight (amos wide)
phrases.notes: Going further than רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.

phrases.english: it also does not need a side post,
whichever way you look at it:
if the standing part is bigger
it is permitted because the standing part is more than the breached part,
and if the breached part is bigger
it (the wall piece) is treated as a side post.
phrases.notes: It must then be less than four אמות, so it qualifies as a לחי.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בְּמָבוֹי שְׁמוֹנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes further than רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's limitation in step 5: even an eight-אמה מבוי needs no extra לחי, which narrows the base rule of step 1 even more.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מבוי eight אמות wide with a wall piece of about four אמות at the entrance needs no extra לחי, because either way it is permitted.

steps.title: What if the wall and the gap are exactly equal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises the third possibility that רב אשי's two options did not cover: the standing part and the open part are exactly the same size.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would you say? That the two are exactly equal to each other?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי, still speaking, raises the one case his מה נפשך has not yet covered: maybe neither side is bigger and they are exactly equal. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's argument covered only two cases, wall bigger or gap bigger. If they are equal, עומד מרובה does not apply, and the wall piece is a full four אמות, which seems too big to be a לחי. So this third case needs its own answer.

keyTerms.meaning: What would you say? This brings up a possible objection in order to answer it.
The two are exactly equal to each other.

phrases.english: What would you say,
that the two of them are equal to each other?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אָמְרַתְּ, דְּשָׁווּ תַּרְוַיְיהוּ כִּי הֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רב אשי's מה נפשך by bringing up the one case it left out.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the law if the standing part and the breached part are exactly equal?

steps.title: An equal case is a rabbinic doubt, so we are lenient
steps.stepSummary: If the two parts are equal, the case is a doubt about a rabbinic law, and we follow the rule ספק דבריהן להקל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then it is a doubt in a rabbinic law, and a doubt in a rabbinic law is ruled leniently.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי finishes his argument by answering the equal case. Since the rules of מבוי are rabbinic, a doubt here is resolved leniently, so the מבוי is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the wall and the gap are equal, we do not know whether to treat the spot as closed or open. Carrying in a מבוי is forbidden only מדרבנן, and in a ספק דרבנן we are lenient. So all three possibilities end with the מבוי permitted, and רב אשי's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt about a law that comes from the חכמים (rabbinic law).
To be lenient.

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי: in an eight-wide מבוי, a four-אמה wall piece is enough. If the wall is bigger, עומד מרובה applies. If the gap is bigger, the wall piece is a לחי. If they are equal, it is a ספק דרבנן, and we are lenient.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think ספק דבריהן להקל applies to every doubt. It works here only because the rules of מבוי are rabbinic. For a doubt in Torah law, we are strict.
steps.whyThisMatters: ספק דרבנן לקולא is a basic rule used all over שס.

phrases.english: it is a doubt in their (rabbinic) words,
and a doubt in rabbinic law is ruled leniently.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָוֵה לֵיהּ סְפֵק דִּבְרֵיהֶן, וּסְפֵק דִּבְרֵיהֶן לְהָקֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the equal-size case raised in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The equal case is a ספק דרבנן, so it is resolved leniently and the מבוי is permitted.

steps.title: New case: an alley that was breached
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new statement from רב חנין בר רבא in the name of רב about a מבוי that got breached.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנין בר רבא said in the name of רב: An alley that was breached...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new topic, a מבוי whose wall got a hole in it. This line only sets up the case, and the ruling comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we have only the opening words and who said them. Wait for the rest before deciding what רב rules about the breach.

keyTerms.meaning: Was breached, had an opening broken into it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָנִין בַּר רָבָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chanin bar Rava said in the name of Rav:
an alley that was breached
phrases.notes: The statement continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָנִין בַּר רָבָא אָמַר רַב: מָבוֹי שֶׁנִּפְרַץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement after the רב אשי discussion is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated. Only the case, a breached מבוי, is introduced here.
